notes: No external resistor: pin 2 uses the internal pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP). Pin 13 drives the onboard LED only, so no external LED or wire is added.
Breadboard bank naming follows the catalogue: 't' is rows a-e and 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the button straddles the centre gap, with its legs in columns 10 and 12 (rows f and e).
The pushbutton's 1.l/1.r are the column-10 legs (joined inside). 2.l/2.r are the column-12 legs. Which leg is called l or r is arbitrary.

The teal wire goes from pin 2 to column 10 (row c). The black wire goes from column 12 (row c) to a GND pin on the power header. I chose GND.2 because the image shows the lower of the two GND pins on that header.
The breadboard power rails are not used.
